events.label: birth
events.text: Sir Samuel Knox Cunningham, 1st Baronet, born.

evidence.quote: Sir Samuel Knox Cunningham , 1st Baronet , QC ( 3 April 1909 – 29 July 1976 )

events.text: Went into business in Northern Ireland.

evidence.quote: From 1931 Cunningham went into business in Northern Ireland

events.text: Married Dorothy Enid Riley, JP.

evidence.quote: He married Dorothy Enid Riley JP on 2 July 1935

events.text: Called to the Bar by the Middle Temple.

evidence.quote: was called to the Bar by the Middle Temple in 1939

events.text: Called to the Bar in Northern Ireland.

evidence.quote: called to the Bar in Northern Ireland in 1942

events.label: election
events.text: Contested the Belfast West by-election.

evidence.quote: He fought the Belfast West by-election in 1943

events.label: election
events.text: Contested the same seat (Belfast West) at the general election.

evidence.quote: and the same seat in the 1945 general election

events.text: Became involved with the World Alliance of YMCAs.

evidence.quote: be involved with the World Alliance of YMCAs from 1947

events.text: Chairman of the National Council of the YMCA.

evidence.quote: Chairman of the National Council of the YMCA in 1949

events.text: Elected to Orpington Urban District Council.

evidence.quote: In 1954 he was elected to Orpington Urban District Council

events.text: Chosen as Ulster Unionist MP for South Antrim.

evidence.quote: In the 1955 general election , Cunningham was chosen as the new Ulster Unionist MP for South Antrim

events.text: Began as delegate to the Council of Europe and WEU Parliamentary Assembly.

evidence.quote: He was a delegate to the Council of Europe and Western European Union Parliamentary Assembly from 1956 to 1959

events.text: Became Parliamentary Private Secretary to Jocelyn Simon.

evidence.quote: He also served as Parliamentary Private Secretary to Jocelyn Simon , Financial Secretary to the Treasury , from 1958

events.label: honour
events.text: Made a Queen's Counsel.

evidence.quote: In 1959 he was made a Queens Counsel

events.text: Picked by Harold Macmillan as Parliamentary Private Secretary.

evidence.quote: After the 1959 general election , Cunningham was picked by Prime Minister Harold Macmillan as his Parliamentary Private Secretary

events.text: Ended delegate role to the Council of Europe and WEU Parliamentary Assembly.

evidence.quote: He was a delegate to the Council of Europe and Western European Union Parliamentary Assembly from 1956 to 1959

events.text: Decided to retire from Parliament at the 1970 general election.

evidence.quote: but decided to retire at the 1970 general election

events.text: Became Provincial Grand Master of the Masonic Order in Gloucestershire.

evidence.quote: He was Provincial Grand Master of the Masonic Order in Gloucestershire from 1970-76

events.text: Became Master of the Drapers Company.

evidence.quote: He was Master of the Drapers Company in 1973–74

events.text: Ended term as Master of the Drapers Company.

evidence.quote: He was Master of the Drapers Company in 1973–74

events.text: Ended term as Provincial Grand Master of the Masonic Order in Gloucestershire.

evidence.quote: He was Provincial Grand Master of the Masonic Order in Gloucestershire from 1970-76

events.label: death
events.text: Died suddenly at Derhams House, Minchinhampton, aged sixty-seven.

evidence.quote: He died suddenly at Derhams House , Minchinhampton on 29 July 1976 at the age of sixty-seven

Heavyweight boxing champion at Clare College (no date)
Later in the 1930s, studied law (decade only)
Served in the Scots Guards during the Second World War (no exact date)
After the war, mainly lived in Orpington (no exact date)
Later maintained a home, Derhams House near Minchinhampton (no date)
Member of the National Executive of the Conservative and Unionist Party (no date)
Awarded a baronetcy in Macmillan's resignation honours (no year stated)
Remained on the backbenches through the rest of the 1960s (decade only)
Member of the Apprentice Boys Club in Derry (no date)
